posts.name: Lalit Kumar
posts.cooked:
Hello , I am trying to create script.sh file but it shows permission denied. Again tried command for creating file with sudo then it says you are not in sudoers file.

2023-03-26_09-11659×396 47.6 KB

How do I fix It? Plz help.

posts.name: Ratheesh
posts.cooked:
Readme says that the assignments have to be done in home folder.
Normal users are not given write permission to /opt folder.

There is folder called ~/se2001 in your home folder. Please use that folder for doing assignments.

@prass Correct me if I am wrong.

posts.name: Sabit sundar Kar
posts.cooked:
Dear Ratheesh,
I am not convinced , as per sample assigment_0 the script.sh is created in side that assigment_0 dir, same should be applicable for rest.
@prass please confirm and assigned the permission for creating script.sh

posts.name: Sanjaykumar
posts.cooked:
Please, read carefully and follow the instructions given for the questions in README.md file.

It is clearly mentioned in README.md that where you have to look for question statement and where to create the solution file.

/opt/se2001 : problem statements directory and not solution directory. So, you don’t need write permission here. Only read permission is sufficient to read the question statement.

~/se2001 : solutions directory, where you have to write your solutions which is defined in problem statements directory.

Please, follow the question statement properly, you will not get stuck. The questions have been cross verified multiple times, so that you will not face any issues.

For any other errors you come across, please raise it on discourse, we will note and act promptly to resolve the errata.

posts.name: Lalit Kumar
posts.cooked:
I created a script.sh file in ~/se2001/assignment_0/ when I am using synchro eval getting evaluation failed error and if executing ~/se2001/assignment_0/script.sh hello.txt
it gives permission denied as you can see in the image below. How do I fix it.

2023-03-26_18-281361×617 86.5 KB

posts.name: MRITYUNJAY KUMAR MISHRA
posts.cooked:
Try running this command in assignment folder source script.sh hello.txt

Kindly check whether the file script.sh have executable permission(s) or not.
use ls -l inside assignment folder

if not then update the permission with this command
chmod +x script.sh

posts.name: Lalit Kumar
posts.cooked:
Now It is working.

What I did here is -

  1. copied the assignment folder from /opt/se2001/<assignment_x> to se2001 directory which is inside my home directory.
  2. Created and written solution in script.sh
  3. Provide executable permissions using chmod +x evaluation.sh script.sh
  4. Executed synchro eval

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked: They are trying to edit a file in /opt/se2001 when instead they should be editting inside ~/se2001. If you’re facing the same error then this is the likely reason.
